chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abdul Jabbar and Al-Razzaz, from Ayoub ibn Nuh, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, who said:
I asked Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) about the man who performs Zahir from his slave girl, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'The free woman and the slave woman are equal in that.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling of Zahir when performed on a slave girl?
ai.summary: In this concise narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that the legal mechanism of *Zahir* (verbal divorce) applies equally to slave women (*Ummahat al-Awlad*) and free women, removing any ambiguity regarding their status in this specific ruling. This establishes a key principle in Shia jurisprudence that the structural validity of *Zahir* is not contingent upon the woman's freedom, though practical implications regarding waiting periods (*Iddah*) may differ. The hadith underscores the consistency of marital dissolution mechanics across social classes within the framework of the Imams' teachings.

en.hubeali: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, and Razzaz, from Ayoub Bin Nuh, from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Is’haq Bin Ammar who said,
‘I asked Abu Ibrahimasws (7th Imamasws) about the man who did Zahaar from his slave girl. So heasws said: ‘The free woman and the slave woman with regards to that, are equal’.
en.sarwar: 11. Abu Ali al-Ash‘ariy has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar and al-Razzaz from Ayyub ibn Nuh from Safwan ibn Yahya from Ishaq ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following:
“I once asked abu Ibrahim, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man who forms al-Zihar about his slave-girl. He (the Imam) said, ‘Free and slaves are the same in al-Zihar.’”
